function_question: How does AI make new pictures and videos?

opening.text: There was a little sketch called Doodle who lived on a page in a drawing book.
Doodle dreamed of dancing, but stuck on the page, it couldn't move a single line.
Doodle wondered: "Animators draw lots of pictures to make things move. What if someone could fill in the pictures between my poses?"

card.place: A page in a drawing book

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: Stuck on the page
chapters.line: Doodle dreams of dancing. Today, YOU get to be the AI that brings it to life.

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Doodle asks for help
chapters.line: Where is a bouncing ball between its start and its landing? Doodle needs a teammate.

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: Predicting what comes next
chapters.line: You and Doodle find out how generative AI makes new things.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of prediction
chapters.line: Generative AI doesn't copy. It predicts.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The sticky-note lab
chapters.line: No magic, just sticky notes! Draw a ball at the top and at the bottom.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The idea storm
chapters.line: What else can AI generate? List as many as you can!

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The storyboard
chapters.line: Three keyframes and a plan for the pictures in between.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: Play it back
chapters.line: Find the jerky moment, predict more frames there, and play again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Doodle is dancing
chapters.line: Doodle bounces and twirls right across the page.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Doodle is stuck on the page, and in-between pictures take ages to draw. Can you be the AI and bring Doodle to life by predicting the frames in between? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some animators already have a plan for the in-betweens. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Generative AI makes new content by predicting what comes next. Tap each card to meet four real-world examples!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four examples share…
guide.skill: Unplugged first! How many in-betweens make the smoothest drop? Predict, then flip your sticky notes.
guide.sketch: Time to storyboard like a real animator!
guide.build_and_test: Add your keyframes and predicted in-betweens in the Animation Studio, then play it. Use drawings or photos of objects only, never faces.
guide.retry_tip: Find the jerkiest moment, predict 2 more frames there, and play it again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Doodle dances across the page, and every frame YOU predicted is proudly labelled, just like AI-made content should be!

quick_check.question: Doodle has 2 keyframes, and you predict 3 in-betweens. How many frames is that altogether?
quick_check.right: Right! 2 + 3 = 5 frames. Shown fast, your brain blends them into motion.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Add the keyframes and the in-betweens together.

clue_cards.name: Cartoon frames
clue_cards.trick: Films are lots of still pictures, called frames.
clue_cards.does: Shown very fast, your brain blends them into motion.

clue_cards.name: Smooth slow motion
clue_cards.trick: AI creates extra frames in between the real ones.
clue_cards.does: A jerky video becomes smooth slow motion.

clue_cards.name: Next-word predictors
clue_cards.trick: It learned patterns from huge amounts of text.
clue_cards.does: It predicts the next word, one word at a time.

clue_cards.name: Picture makers
clue_cards.trick: It learned patterns from millions of example pictures.
clue_cards.does: It creates new pictures, but can make mistakes, like extra fingers!

predict.prompt: Should it be labelled as AI-generated? Predict first!

predict.explain: AI predicts new frames and pictures, so it can make mistakes and make fake things look real. Anything AI made gets a label. Idea Pop does this too!

lab.title: The sticky-note lab
lab.predict: How many in-between frames make the smoothest ball drop?

tool.name: Brainstorm
tool.intro: Brainstorming is how teams find lots of ideas fast, then pick the best ones. Today you'll use all 5 rules to explore what AI can generate.

parts.name: Quantity
parts.what: Go for lots of ideas, fast.
parts.example: 🥤 20 uses for a cup in 5 minutes: seed pot, phone speaker…
parts.starter: Things AI can generate or predict: words, music, pictures, weather…

parts.name: No Judging
parts.what: Every idea is allowed for now.
parts.example: 🥤 A cup hat? Write it down anyway!
parts.starter: An odd idea I'll still write down is AI that makes…

parts.name: Wild ideas
parts.what: Be brave and try something unusual.
parts.example: 🥤 A tower of 1,000 cups that plays music!
parts.starter: My wildest idea is an AI that predicts…

parts.name: Build on ideas
parts.what: Take an idea and add to it.
parts.example: 🥤 A seed pot → a seed pot with a drip hole.
parts.starter: AI that makes pictures could become AI that…

parts.name: Pick the best
parts.what: Choose the ideas that matter most.
parts.example: 🥤 Keep the idea that's cheapest and most useful.
parts.starter: I'll star the ones where a mistake could fool people, and label them by…

sketch_checklist: I drew 3 keyframes for one simple action.
I marked how many in-betweens go between each pair.
I wrote the pattern I'll follow, like "slower at the top".

test.check_question: Could a friend tell which frames were keyframes and which were predicted?

reflection.question: AI check: why is it important to label pictures and videos made by AI?
options: 🤝 To be honest about who made it
🏷️ So people can check before they trust it
